alerts.title: Carbamazepine-DTG interaction lowers DTG levels
alerts.message: Guidelines state carbamazepine decreases DTG levels by 30–70% and advise using valproic acid instead. Patient started carbamazepine 2 weeks ago while on DTG-based TLD. Viral load rose from <50 to 1,240 copies/mL despite reported good adherence, consistent with reduced DTG exposure. The clinician's plan addresses carbamazepine toxicity but does not address the pharmacokinetic interaction causing virological failure. Switching from carbamazepine to valproic acid (already prescribed) would resolve both toxicity and the interaction.

evidence.recommended_action: Replace carbamazepine with valproic acid monotherapy per guidelines. Repeat viral load after switching to confirm re-suppression.

alerts.title: Carbamazepine toxicity with hyponatremia
alerts.message: Patient has carbamazepine level 14 mcg/mL (therapeutic 4–12), with nystagmus, ataxia, and tremor. Hyponatremia (Na 128 mmol/L) is also consistent with carbamazepine-induced SIADH. The plan to reduce dose and repeat the level is appropriate. Concurrent valproate may also contribute to CNS toxicity. Non-drug causes of hyponatremia (dehydration, infection) should be excluded. ALT 68 U/L may reflect hepatic effects of carbamazepine, valproate, or both antiepileptics combined.

evidence.recommended_action: Reduce carbamazepine dose, repeat level and sodium. Monitor LFTs. Consider replacing carbamazepine with valproate to eliminate interaction.

alerts.title: Detectable viral load requires adherence counselling
alerts.message: Guidelines state virological monitoring provides early indication of treatment failure and need to switch therapy. Patient's viral load became detectable at 1,240 copies/mL after suppression. While the carbamazepine-DTG interaction is the likely cause, guidelines recommend adherence counselling and repeat viral load before confirming treatment failure. The clinician's plan does not include adherence counselling or a repeat viral load strategy.

evidence.recommended_action: Provide adherence counselling, address carbamazepine-DTG interaction, and repeat viral load in 2–3 months to assess re-suppression.

alerts.title: Elevated ALT with dual hepatotoxic antiepileptics
alerts.message: Guidelines advise performing LFTs when TDF toxicity is suspected and monitoring for hepatotoxicity. ALT is 68 U/L (approximately grade 1 elevation). Both carbamazepine and valproate are known hepatotoxins; combined use compounds risk. TDF can also cause hepatic steatosis. Evidence against drug attribution: ALT is only mildly elevated and no other TDF toxicity signs are present. However, dual antiepileptic therapy warrants ongoing LFT monitoring.

evidence.recommended_action: Repeat ALT within 2–4 weeks. If rising, consider simplifying antiepileptic regimen and evaluate TDF contribution.
